text: ggincerta extension ggplot2 visualising uncertainty spatial data , generally, constructing bivariate visualisations. reimplements visualisation methods three map types introduced Vizumap package within grammar graphics, also providing additional uncertainty visualisation approaches. package integrates directly ggplot2 custom scales, geoms, aesthetics, guides. allows uncertainty visualisations constructed, combined, customised using workflow conventional ggplot2 graphics.

title: Extend ggplot2 with Layers and Scales for Spatial Uncertainty Visualization
text: ggincerta provides scale_*_bivariate() constructing bivariate colour scales can used duo() inside ggplot2 aesthetics. Two variables discretised independently, crossed bin combinations mapped two-dimensional colour grid. default, automatically generated breaks use breaks_pretty() transformed scale. n_breaks argument specifies desired number bins, nice.breaks = TRUE, actual number bins may differ order produce readable break values.  exact number equal-width bins required, set nice.breaks = FALSE. Quantile-based binning also available setting quantile = TRUE.  default palette generated mixing two colour ramps. Alternative palette functions can supplied palette_fun. example, bivar_fade_palette() can used emphasise one variable progressively suppressing another perceptual dimension along second axis.  complete control colour grid, ggincerta also provides manual bivariate scales. Manual scales use exact equal-width bins default, number required colours determined directly n_breaks. Value-Suppressing Uncertainty Palettes (VSUPs), proposed Correll et al. (2018), suppress value differences uncertainty increases. ggincerta, implemented scale_*_vsup(). uncertainty variable divided hierarchy layers, number value bins varies across layers according branch parameter. breaks supplied, value uncertainty breaks generated equal-width intervals transformed scale.  Custom breaks limits can also supplied explicitly.
code: ggplot(nc) + geom_sf(aes(fill = duo(value, sd))) ggplot(nc) +   geom_sf(aes(fill = duo(value, sd))) +   scale_fill_bivariate(     n_breaks = 4,     nice.breaks = FALSE   ) ggplot(nc) +   geom_sf(aes(fill = duo(value, sd))) +   scale_fill_bivariate(     palette_fun = bivar_fade_palette,     colours = c("#F6E8C3", "orange", "red"),     palette_params = list(fade = "desaturate")   ) ggplot(nc) +   geom_sf(aes(fill = duo(value, sd))) +   scale_fill_vsup() ggplot(nc) +   geom_sf(aes(fill = duo(value, sd))) +   scale_fill_vsup(     breaks = list(       seq(-3, 3, length.out = 9),       seq(0, 4, length.out = 5)     ),     limits = list(       c(-3, 3),       c(0, 4)     )   ) +   theme(     legend.text = element_text(size = 7)   )

title: Extend ggplot2 with Layers and Scales for Spatial Uncertainty Visualization
text: ggincerta provides geom_sf_pixel() constructing pixel maps. spatial unit tessellated pixels, pixel values sampled specified probability distribution parameterised mapped variables. Pixel grids can generated using rectangular, square, hexagonal cells, hexagonal pixels used default. Variation pixel colours within region provides visual representation uncertainty retaining spatial pattern underlying estimate. pixel generation relies geometric intersection, computation can slower working directly geographic sf objects s2 geometry system. improved performance, recommended first transform data projected planar coordinate reference system.  pixel shape resolution can also customised pixel_shape.
code: nc_flat <- sf::st_transform(nc, 3857)  ggplot(nc_flat) +   geom_sf_pixel(     mapping = aes(fill = duo_pixel(value, sd)),     seed = 123   ) ggplot(nc_flat) +   geom_sf_pixel(     mapping = aes(fill = duo_pixel(value, sd)),     pixel_shape = "square",     n = 30,     seed = 123   )

title: Extend ggplot2 with Layers and Scales for Spatial Uncertainty Visualization
text: Glyph maps use additional graphical marks placed spatial centroids represent value uncertainty. ggincerta provides several glyph forms geom_sf_glyph(). Regular shapes circles, squares, triangles, hexagons can used bivariate colour scales.  Drop-shaped glyphs provide alternative encoding uncertainty can represented rotation angle aesthetic.  Chernoff faces provide another glyph form multivariate encoding. implementation ggincerta builds grob scale design provided ggChernoff package. example , facial colour represents estimated value, facial expression represents uncertainty: lower uncertainty produces smiling faces, whereas higher uncertainty produces frowning faces.
code: ggplot(nc_flat) +   geom_sf_glyph(     mapping = aes(colour = duo(value, sd))   ) #> Warning: st_point_on_surface assumes attributes are constant over geometries ggplot(nc_flat) +   geom_sf_glyph(     aes(colour = value, angle = sd),     shape = "drop"   ) #> Warning: st_point_on_surface assumes attributes are constant over geometries ggplot(nc_flat) +   geom_sf_glyph(     aes(colour = value, smile = sd),     shape = "chernoff"   )

title: Extend ggplot2 with Layers and Scales for Spatial Uncertainty Visualization
text: dual map combines conventional choropleth layer glyph layer spatial display. two layers can use separate aesthetics, scales, guides, allowing primary variable uncertainty remain visually distinct directly interpretable. simple dual map can, example, map uncertainty polygon fill estimated value glyph colour.  choropleth glyph components layered within ggplot2 system, can also combined bivariate mappings. makes possible encode additional variable duo() retaining separate glyph-based representation.
code: ggplot(nc_flat) +   geom_sf_dualmap(     aes(fill = sd, colour = value)   ) #> Warning: st_point_on_surface assumes attributes are constant over geometries ggplot(nc_flat) +   geom_sf_dualmap(     aes(       fill = duo(value, sd),       colour = value     )   ) +   scale_colour_gradient(low = "grey95", high = "grey40") +   scale_fill_bivariate() #> Warning: st_point_on_surface assumes attributes are constant over geometries
